overview: CarMax is the largest retailer of used vehicles in the United States, operating 258 no-haggle used car stores plus a nationwide omni-channel platform (CarMax.com, mobile app, Edmunds) that lets customers buy, sell or finance a car online, in-store, or a mix of both. The company runs two reportable segments: CarMax Sales Operations (retail and wholesale vehicle sales, extended protection plans, and Edmunds advertising/subscription revenue) and CarMax Auto Finance (CAF), its captive, full-credit-spectrum auto lender. It is also one of the largest wholesale vehicle auction operators in the country, reselling appraisal purchases that do not meet its retail standards.

business_model.summary: CarMax buys and reconditions used vehicles for retail sale at fixed, no-haggle prices, disposing of vehicles that don't meet retail standards through its own wholesale auctions. It captures additional economics by financing roughly 40% of retail sales through CAF and selling extended protection plans (EPP) on behalf of third parties. Revenue is almost entirely transactional/unit-driven rather than recurring, though the growing CAF loan book and EPP attachment provide an annuity-like profit stream layered on top of each vehicle sale.
business_model.customer_type: B2C retail consumers (used vehicle buyers/sellers across the full credit spectrum) plus B2B licensed dealers who buy at CarMax's wholesale auctions and use its MaxOffer appraisal tool
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% United States; 258 stores in 111 television markets covering ~85% of the U.S. population (FY2026/Q2 FY2027)

competitive_position.market_position: Largest used vehicle retailer and one of the largest wholesale auction operators and used-vehicle lenders in the U.S., but still only ~3.6% of the ~20 million 0-10 year old used vehicles sold nationally in calendar 2025 (down from 3.7% in 2024) in a highly fragmented market with no dominant player.

moat_factors.description: High-volume appraisal process (1.1M vehicles purchased in FY2026) sources inventory more cheaply than auctions and feeds a captive wholesale auction business with a ~99% sales rate
No-haggle pricing, 10-day money-back guarantee and 30-day warranty differentiate from traditional dealer negotiation model; 22 consecutive years on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For
Decades of transaction data feed proprietary inventory, pricing and CAF underwriting algorithms (99% of retail inventory sells at retail)
In-house lender optimized for the CarMax customer captures finance economics third-party lenders would otherwise keep; CAF penetration expanding into Tier 2/3 full-spectrum lending
Nationwide inventory transfer network (38% of vehicles sold are transferred on request) gives customers far more selection than a single-lot dealer

weaknesses: No long-term exclusivity or switching costs — customers can and do shop Carvana, dealers and private sellers for the same vehicle with one click
Market share has stagnated/declined slightly as online-native competitors (notably Carvana) and dealer groups invest heavily in their own digital experiences
Thin net margins on vehicle sales make results highly sensitive to used-vehicle pricing swings and SG&A leverage
CAF's expansion into Tier 2/3 lending increases credit risk exposure precisely as it chases growth
Recent leadership upheaval (abrupt CEO departure, new outside CEO from hospitality) creates strategic and execution uncertainty

growth_drivers: "Shift into GEAR" strategy (Great Offering, Easy Experience, Add Value, Run Lean) under new CEO Keith Barr aimed at reaccelerating unit and earnings growth

CAF full-credit-spectrum lending expansion — Tier 2 origination target raised to ~30% of Tier 2 volume in FY2027 from <15% in FY2026, each incremental point of CAF penetration estimated to add $10-12M of lifetime pre-tax income
Extended protection plan (EPP) redesign rolling out nationwide in FY2027, targeted to add ~$35/unit of incremental EPP margin
$200 million SG&A exit-rate cost savings target by end of FY2027 (raised from $150 million), with full earnings benefit expected in FY2028
Continued store/capacity expansion — stand-alone reconditioning and auction centers to balance capacity, plus selective new store openings (258 stores as of Q2 FY2027)
Scaling AI/agentic tools (e.g., Skye virtual assistant, AI voice across call centers) to lower reconditioning/operating costs and improve conversion
Resumption of share buybacks in Q3 FY2027 ($1.31B of $2.0B authorization remaining) as leverage normalizes
Large total addressable market: ~39 million used vehicles sold annually in the U.S. with no single competitor holding more than mid-single-digit share

business.description: Carvana's omni-channel model, franchised dealers' certified-pre-owned programs, AutoNation/Lithia dealer groups, and private-party/online facilitation tools all compete for the same vehicles and customers
Estimated national share of 0-10 year old used vehicles fell to 3.6% in CY2025 from 3.7% in CY2024, with share pressured in the back half of the year
Steep swings in wholesale values can compress retail and wholesale margins and strand inventory

business.risk: Dependence on third-party finance and EPP providers
business.description: Significant share of financing and all EPP products are sourced from third parties (Ally, Capital One, Santander, Assurant, Fidelity, etc.); loss of a key partner could hurt sales

financial.description: Allowance for loan losses rose to 3.07% of loans held for investment as of Aug 2026 as CAF expands into higher-risk Tier 2 lending; FY2026 provision reflected unfavorable performance on 2022-2023 vintage loans
CAF funds most originations through warehouse facilities and term securitizations; disruption in ABS markets could force curtailment of lending
Net leverage above targeted range forced a pause in share buybacks through fiscal 2026; debt load includes ~$17.4 billion of total debt (mostly non-recourse notes) as of Aug 2026
FY2026 results included a goodwill impairment charge (related to Edmunds) that contributed to a 50.6% drop in GAAP net earnings

regulatory.description: CAF financing activity is subject to CFPB, FTC, truth-in-lending, fair credit reporting and state installment-finance laws; violations could bring fines or license revocation
Operations require state/local dealer, finance and sales licenses; non-compliance risk in a highly regulated industry
Enhanced FTC focus on all-in advertised pricing has so far been a tailwind for CarMax's transparent no-haggle model relative to competitors, but rule changes could cut both ways

macro.description: Rates affect CAF's funding costs and margin, as well as consumers' ability to afford financed vehicle payments; weighted average contract rate rose to 11.8% in Q2 FY2027
Unemployment, inflation and consumer sentiment directly affect vehicle affordability, loan performance and recovery rates at auction
Tariffs on vehicles, parts and steel can raise acquisition and construction costs and disrupt the supply of late-model used vehicles via reduced new vehicle production

execution.description: Former CEO Bill Nash departed abruptly in November 2025 after a weak Q3 FY2026 outlook; new CEO Keith Barr (ex-IHG, hospitality background, no prior auto retail experience) started March 2026 and is still formulating long-term strategy, with a fuller plan unveiled at a November 3, 2026 strategic update

Consolidated class action (Cap v. CarMax, transferred to E.D. Va.) alleges the company overstated growth prospects and that sales strength reflected tariff-driven pull-forward demand ahead of the CEO's departure; outcome and damages are not yet estimable
In-process pension termination expected to result in ~$50 million of settlement charges in fiscal 2027

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The U.S. used vehicle market is large (~39 million units sold in calendar 2025) and highly fragmented, with over 18,000 franchised dealers plus independents and online players; industry adoption of digital/omni-channel buying continues to grow, and CAF's consumer finance sector represents roughly $1.7 trillion in outstanding receivables
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — used vehicle sales and financing are sensitive to consumer discretionary spending, employment, credit availability and vehicle affordability; FY2026 showed declining comparable sales while Q2 FY2027 showed a sharp rebound
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — both CAF funding costs/margins and customer loan affordability move with benchmark rates (SOFR); the company uses interest rate swaps to hedge a portion of securitization funding costs
key_input_costs: Steel and construction costs for new stores/auction facilities

recent_developments.event: CEO Bill Nash stepped down (effective Dec 1, 2025) following a weak preliminary Q3 FY2026 outlook; stock fell as much as ~20-24% and multiple securities class-action suits were filed alleging the company overstated growth tied to tariff-driven demand pull-forward
CarMax named Keith Barr, former CEO of InterContinental Hotels Group, as President and CEO effective March 16, 2026, succeeding interim CEO David McCreight (who became non-executive Board Chair)

FY2026 results showed GAAP net earnings down 50.6% to $247.3M (diluted EPS $1.68, -47.7%) and adjusted EPS of $2.91 (-11.0%), impacted by a goodwill impairment charge and CEO-transition/restructuring costs; share buybacks were paused in Q4 FY2026 as leverage ran above target

Revenue grew 19.5% to $7.88 billion and diluted EPS rose 81.3% to $1.16, beating analyst estimates (~$0.73 EPS, ~$7.03B revenue consensus); comparable store used unit sales rose 13.0%; CAF income rose 32.1% aided by a $16.6M gain on a non-prime loan sale

Despite the earnings beat, shares were volatile as investors weighed cautious commentary on used vehicle margins, CAF income guided slightly lower for the full year, and the pace of planned buyback resumption
Held a virtual 'fall strategic update' laying out further details, multi-year targets and milestones for the "Shift into GEAR" growth strategy
Company plans to resume share repurchases in Q3 FY2027 at a modest pace (below its pre-pause average) after improving leverage to the upper end of its targeted range

Analyst sentiment has turned more constructive after the Q2 beat — JPMorgan and Barclays both raised price targets to roughly $60 (from $38 and $26 respectively) — though consensus remains a cautious Hold with wide dispersion (~$35-$66) given lingering competitive and credit concerns highlighted by Evercore ISI's downgrade to In Line

items.metric: Used vehicle gross profit per unit
items.target: decline less than $200/unit year-over-year, full fiscal year
items.notes: Improved from the 10-K's original guidance of a decline 'broadly in line with the Q4 FY2026 year-over-year trend' (as much as ~$300/unit in Q1); management says it lowered margins less than the prior $200/unit outlook in Q2 as it balanced demand and efficiency gains

items.target: $200 million in exit-rate savings by end of FY2027
items.period: FY2027 exit rate / full benefit in FY2028
items.notes: Raised earlier in FY2026 from an original $150M target; ~half of in-year savings offset by annualizing lower FY2026 incentive/share-based compensation; company reaffirmed it remains on track, with ~$6M of incremental severance in Q3 FY2027
From the nationwide EPP product redesign rollout (completed ~October 2026); EPP margin was already up $27/unit in H1 FY2027
Despite a strong Q2 (CAF income +32.1%), full-year guide reflects lower average loans outstanding following prior-year loan sales and continued Tier 2 credit mix shift
H1 FY2027 interest margin was 6.7%, up from 6.5% in H1 FY2026, aided by higher-margin Tier 2 loans
Up from a <15% target in FY2026 as part of the full-credit-spectrum lending expansion; H1 FY2027 actual was ~23%
Down from $541.0 million in FY2026 as new-store growth slows and offsite reconditioning/auction investment moderates

items.target: 1 additional store, 1 stand-alone auction facility, 1 stand-alone reconditioning/auction center for the remainder of FY2027
items.notes: 258 stores in 111 TV markets as of Q2 FY2027, covering ~85% of the U.S. population; one additional store opened in Austin, TX after quarter-end

items.target: resume in Q3 FY2027 at a modest pace, below pre-pause average
items.notes: Buybacks were paused in Q4 FY2026 due to elevated leverage; $1.31 billion remains available under the $2.0 billion board authorization

items.target: expect to leverage (improve) year-over-year, excluding FY2026 restructuring charges
items.notes: SG&A per total unit already down 8.8% and 7.7% in Q2 and H1 FY2027, respectively

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Keith Barr has framed fiscal 2027 around a four-pillar 'Shift into GEAR' strategy (Great Offering, Easy Experience, Add Value, Run Lean), emphasizing competitive no-haggle pricing, faster inventory access, digital/AI-enabled experience improvements, CAF full-spectrum lending, EPP margin redesign, and reconditioning/logistics cost reduction. Management says it is 'encouraged' that H1 FY2027 trends (mid-single-digit unit growth, SG&A leverage, higher CAF Tier 2 penetration, higher EPP margin, improving EPS) will continue, and detailed further multi-year milestones at a November 3, 2026 virtual strategic update. CFO commentary flags that corporate incentive compensation dynamics will keep pressuring the SG&A savings comparison through Q3 FY2027 before moderating in Q4.

bull_case: Clear evidence of an operational turnaround under new CEO Keith Barr: Q2 FY2027 revenue grew 19.5%, diluted EPS grew 81.3%, and comparable store used units grew 13.0%, meaningfully beating analyst estimates

CAF's full-credit-spectrum lending expansion (Tier 2 target raised to ~30% of volume) and the EPP redesign (+$35/unit target) are largely untapped, high-margin profit levers layered on top of an already-leading retail franchise
$200 million SG&A exit-rate savings target plus falling capital expenditure needs ($400M vs. $541M in FY2026) should expand earnings leverage as sales recover
Still only ~3.6% national share of a highly fragmented, ~39-million-unit used vehicle market gives a long runway for share gains if the new strategy executes

Capital returns resuming — buybacks restart in Q3 FY2027 with $1.31 billion of authorization remaining — and several analysts (JPMorgan, Barclays) have recently raised price targets meaningfully on the turnaround narrative
bear_case: Unresolved securities class-action litigation tied to the abrupt CEO departure and allegations that FY2026 sales strength was driven by unsustainable, tariff-related pull-forward demand creates legal and reputational overhang
New CEO comes from hospitality (IHG), not automotive retail or consumer finance, raising execution risk as the company builds out a still-forming long-term strategy
Expanding CAF into higher-risk Tier 2/3 lending to chase growth increases credit exposure just as the allowance for loan losses is already rising (3.07% of loans held for investment as of Aug 2026)
Competitive intensity is rising from Carvana's omni-channel model and dealer groups (AutoNation, Lithia), and CarMax's own national market share slipped to 3.6% in CY2025 from 3.7% in CY2024

Business remains highly cyclical and rate-sensitive — used vehicle affordability, consumer credit conditions and wholesale values can swing results sharply, as shown by the FY2026 goodwill impairment and 50.6% GAAP earnings decline; analyst consensus remains a cautious Hold with a wide target range ($35-$66)
